description: You are a traffic signal engineer at the Municipality of Bologna's Mobility Department (Settore Mobilita). The Acosta corridor experiences severe congestion due to poorly coordinated traffic signals along the main arterial route. Your task is to implement a 'green wave' (onda verde) by optimizing signal offsets along the corridor so that vehicles traveling at the design speed encounter consecutive green lights. Using the Bologna Acosta scenario at /home/ga/SUMO_Scenarios/bologna_acosta/: (1) Run the baseline simulation (using the existing run.sumocfg) and save the tripinfo output. Then compute corridor-level performance metrics from the tripinfo: average travel time, average waiting time, and average time loss for all vehicles. Save these baseline metrics to /home/ga/SUMO_Output/baseline_corridor_metrics.csv with columns: metric,value (rows: avg_travel_time_s, avg_waiting_time_s, avg_time_loss_s, total_vehicles). (2) Analyze the existing traffic light programs in acosta_tls.add.xml. Identify the signal cycle lengths and compute appropriate offsets for at least 4 of the 7 signalized intersections (TLS IDs: 209, 210, 219, 220, 221, 235, 273) to create progressive signal coordination. Create a modified TLS additional file at /home/ga/SUMO_Scenarios/bologna_acosta/acosta_tls_coordinated.add.xml with adjusted offset values. The offsets should be computed based on inter-intersection distances and a design speed (50 km/h urban arterial). (3) Create a modified simulation configuration at /home/ga/SUMO_Scenarios/bologna_acosta/run_coordinated.sumocfg that uses your coordinated TLS file instead of the original. Run the coordinated simulation and save its tripinfo output. (4) Compute the same corridor metrics for the coordinated simulation and save to /home/ga/SUMO_Output/coordinated_corridor_metrics.csv (same format). (5) Produce a coordination assessment report at /home/ga/SUMO_Output/signal_coordination_report.txt documenting: the offset values chosen for each intersection and the rationale, before/after comparison of corridor metrics, percentage improvements achieved, and professional recommendations for implementation.
